summary: Every node must be classified and the contract requires arbitrary node values in ascending order, matching one parent-set construction plus the final result sort.

optimality.argument: All n nodes produce output rows whose arbitrary numeric values must be ordered; comparison ordering requires Omega(n log n), while parent membership is linear with hashing and the final sort is O(n log n).

replacement_checks.evidence: The required output contains all n arbitrary node values in ascending numeric order.
A parent-value set supports linear classification, followed by one O(n log n) ordering step.
Cases cover singleton, chain, sparse IDs, balanced and unbalanced roles, null semantics, and numeric order.
